# Once More, From the Top

J-pop / anisong sketch in D major at 152 BPM in 4/4, 32 bars with a final chorus a whole step up in E. A D7 (V/IV) turnaround loops back to the hook-first intro.

## Form

| Section | Bars | Chords | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intro (hook) | 1–4 | Gmaj7 A7–F♯m7 Bm7–Em7 A7–Gmaj7 A7sus4 A7 | Chorus hook first, piano, 8th-note arp, light drums |
| Verse | 5–12 | D–A/C♯–Bm7–Gmaj7–Em7–F♯m7–Gmaj7–A7sus4 A7 | Low melody, one chord per bar, strings from bar 9 |
| Pre-chorus | 13–16 | Em7 A7–F♯m7 B7–Gmaj7 F♯7–Bm7 E7 A7sus4 A7 | Harmonic rhythm speeds up, snare build roll |
| Chorus | 17–24 | Gmaj7 A7 F♯m7 Bm7–Em7 A7–D D7, then Gmaj7 A7–F♯7 Bm7–Em7 A7sus4 A7–D B7 | Royal road, melody lifts to D6, B7 pivots to E |
| Final chorus (E) | 25–32 | Royal road in E, ending E D7 | Violin countermelody, 16th arp and hats, peak at E6 |

## Harmony

- The chorus uses the royal road (IVmaj7–V7–iii7–vi) with secondary dominants: D7 = V/IV, B7 = V/ii, F♯7 = V/vi, E7 = V/V.
- B7 is V/ii in D and becomes the dominant of E for the key change.
- Melodies push off the beat: verse phrases start on the "&" of 1, and chorus notes anticipate the barline.
